scores.quote: we have large feet on street, we have initiatives that we run quarter -on-quarter

scores.rationale: The benefit mix is well matched to a retail/prescriber customer base — brand recall and field-force reach rather than TCO arguments — though the model carries no corporate-style switching-cost lock-in.
scores.quote: It's not sold to the doctor's prescription , but they do have a very good brand recall

scores.rationale: R&D intensity of 4-5% supports a real multi-platform capability — biosimilars, Enzene bio-CDMO and Occlutech's nitinol occluder platform with in-house labs and clean rooms — but it is fast-follower rather than proprietary innovation.
scores.quote: this company has a very strong R&D setup with their own research lab, multiple research lab, own clean room

scores.rationale: No evidence of any two-sided or self-reinforcing network is discussed in any of the calls.

Distribution reach is the durable edge — pioneer status and unmatched stockist relationships in trade generics plus a top-five prescription field force that rivals entering the space must build from scratch.
scores.quote: The relationship we enjoy with the stock ist fraternity is kind of unparalleled

scores.rationale: Capex is genuinely growth-oriented and delivered on time/budget (Rs 400cr ethylamine plant, Rs 120cr Kurkumbh new product, new Dahej product), but incremental returns have been poor — the big ethylamine plant sits at 60-70% utilisation years later, guided asset turn is only ~1.5x, and topline has been flat for three years.
scores.quote: we should be at about 60%-70% utilization in that plant. There is plenty of headroom to go further.

scores.rationale: No mention of advertising or promotional spend across any of the eight calls — it is a B2B chemicals business with no A&P discussion.

R&D consistently yields commercialised, self-developed import-substitute products and continuous yield/consumption improvements, but conversion is slow — the Rs 600-800cr new-product revenue promised in 2022 has not shown up in a flat topline by FY26.
scores.quote: barring the initial technologies which we imported from America, all the products we have launched in the last 35-40 years have been with our own R&D and engineering efforts

scores.rationale: No acquisitions discussed or contemplated in any call; growth is entirely organic greenfield/brownfield capex.
Buybacks, dividends or any distribution policy are not discussed anywhere in the excerpts.

Capital-heavy chemical plants running at 60-85% utilisation with new capex guided at only ~1.5x asset turn, and the 'moat' is weak enough that Chinese imports and a fourth domestic methylamine entrant compress returns.
scores.quote: About 1.5 turnover, it is, turnover-to-asset ratio.

scores.rationale: Modest but real share capture — acetonitrile share rising post anti-dumping duty and overall share retained/slightly increased in FY26 — though methylamine volumes were lost to competition.
scores.quote: we have managed to retain and perhaps even slightly increase our market share in various markets that we operate in

scores.rationale: Export mix has been static at roughly 20% for years with no geographic expansion programme, and the only international exposure discussed (US, ~1% of topline) was a source of damage rather than growth.
scores.quote: Even the domestic export sectors are more or less the same 80-20.

scores.rationale: Growth is volume-led at best and pricing is pure raw-material pass-through in a commodity market — FY26 saw both price and volume fall ~1% each, and earlier price rises were explicitly input-cost driven.
scores.quote: prices have dropped 1% and volume has probably dropped 1%

scores.rationale: Company appears near a cyclical trough with identifiable catalysts ahead — acetonitrile anti-dumping duty now effective, China 'anti-involution' capacity cuts, and management's own view that the worst is past.
scores.quote: we are optimistic that we have seen probably the worst, and we hope to see better times in the future

scores.rationale: Core end-markets (pharma/life sciences at 65-70% of sales, agrochemicals) are structurally growing, with an incremental secular driver in GLP-1 peptide APIs using acetonitrile, though management sizes this at only ~10% of a 30,000t market.
scores.quote: acetonitrile is used in the API. So, it is used in most of the peptide drugs

scores.rationale: Strictly organic growth with no M&A, projects delivered 'well within budget', counter-cyclical investment continued through a three-year downturn, and explicit willingness to defer further capex until volatility settles.
scores.quote: we have got them on to engineering stage, but we will take a final decision on whether to invest or not into this after this volatility in the market settles

scores.rationale: Consistently long-horizon and independent — decade-scale plant decisions, 4-5 year product gestation, self-developed technology, and refusal to enter DMF or upstream ammonia simply because peers do.
scores.quote: It takes almost 4 to 5 years from conceptualization to come to the bench trial to engineering

scores.rationale: Deliberately low-profile: refuses to name unlaunched products, declines to disclose volumes or customer-wise sales, no promotional framing, and calls are handled soberly by the same executive director and CFO across four years.
scores.quote: we do not talk about the products which we are going to launch until they are actually commercially in the field. That's our policy.

scores.rationale: Some evidence of institutional capability-building (dedicated process engineering group, R&D group, addition of a Chief Commercial Officer), but no articulated talent-development system and notable churn at the top with Kothari's exit and multiple chairman changes.
scores.quote: we have a separate team, which we call the process engineering group

scores.rationale: Consistently candid across the cycle — openly enumerated four distinct ways US policy hurt them, admitted guidance misses on volume, and acknowledged DEK and Monoisopropylamine underperformance rather than deflecting.
scores.quote: So, we have been affected in four ways by these actions of the US government

scores.rationale: Management itself separates luck from skill — explicitly treating the COVID windfall as off-trend rather than as evidence of capability — which makes an unhaloed assessment possible, though weak three-year results temper any inference of superior skill.
scores.quote: that COVID year was off the trend line, and we are now on the trend line

scores.rationale: Holds niche near-monopoly positions — sole Indian producer of pharma-grade acetonitrile (with caveat that others process it) and sole domestic maker of the new import-substitute dyes/electronics product — but the bulk amine business has no such position.
scores.quote: Import-substitute; there is nobody in the country making this.

scores.rationale: Little evidence of switching costs — customers freely substitute cheaper Chinese imports, and even acetonitrile quality differentiation is still 'being worked on' rather than established as a lock-in.
scores.quote: for most part of the applications, both routes are acceptable to the customers

scores.rationale: Mixed structure: ethylamines is a rational, stable duopoly with protected margins, but methylamines has degraded to four players with ~150,000t capacity against 80,000-90,000t demand.
scores.quote: Ethyl has been only 2 of us, Balaji and us in the market. And there has been a somewhat stable market share kind of rationing

scores.rationale: Entry barriers proved insufficient — Aarti Drugs commissioned a new methylamine plant creating structural overhang, and Chinese players priced below cost, forcing reliance on anti-dumping duties rather than industry rationality.
scores.quote: there is a capacity of more than 1,50,000 tons in the market, which can all come on stream

scores.rationale: Imports are the clear donator pool — roughly 40% of the acetonitrile market was imported, and share has begun shifting to Alkyl as anti-dumping duty bites and Chinese aggression eases.
scores.quote: they have reduced their imports because they have raised their prices. So more and more, our market share has been increasing.

scores.rationale: The aliphatic amines niche is small and management is unshowy, but the obscurity is not protective — the stock is covered by HDFC, Ambit, Motilal and Marcellus and the niche has attracted both a new domestic entrant and heavy Chinese capacity.
scores.quote: now we have a fourth player coming into the market, Aarti Drugs

scores.rationale: No image- or taste-based pricing power; this is a commodity where realisations track raw materials and competitor behaviour, with finished-goods prices falling 5-6% and margins described as multi-decade lows.
scores.quote: the finished good prices have dropped a little more than the raw material prices... the margins have got squeezed

scores.rationale: Some genuine trust/qualification value — pharma-grade purity, customer approvals for peptide manufacture, and a Responsible Care commitment — which gives reliability-based stickiness even if price still dominates.
scores.quote: We have got some approvals from some of these manufacturers for our acetonitrile

scores.rationale: Serves ~200 pharma customers directly with domestic supply proximity versus imports, but there is no evidence of superior accessibility or a differentiated sales force, and its distributor chain proved a vulnerability under sanctions.
scores.quote: maybe about 200 customers in the pharma business

scores.rationale: Correctly matched to an industrial customer base — the product is a low-share 'C item' in customers' cost structure, which supports cost pass-through and reliability-based purchasing rather than intangibles.
scores.quote: we are actually a very minor cost in their cost of material. It's what you might call a C item.

scores.rationale: Real but narrow technology edge — all products over 35-40 years developed in-house, continuous yield and specific-consumption gains, and claimed process superiority on the new Kurkumbh product — yet it has not prevented price erosion from Chinese competition.
scores.quote: we feel that our technology will be superior to that, and we will be able to maintain this

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network is present or discussed in any of the calls.

Distribution is mentioned only as a vulnerability rather than an advantage — sanctions on Indian distributors in its supply chain were cited as one of four hits to the business — with no evidence of unmatchable reach or service.
scores.quote: the sanctions on some of our distributors in India who are part of our supply chain

scores.rationale: Sustained, large growth capex (Sri City greenfield, Sidwal greenfield, >INR4,500cr ECMS PCB approvals, INR350-375cr annual guidance) but incremental returns lag — the 19-21% ROCE promise has been repeatedly pushed out since FY23.
scores.quote: we have got more than INR4,500 crores total investment approvals under ECMS for Ascent-K Circuit in Noida for HDI PCB

scores.rationale: Pure B2B/ODM model; no A&P spend or brand-building discussion in any excerpt.

R&D has repeatedly converted into first-to-market products and new customers — India's first in-house inverter PCB, first B2B ODM tower/cassette/window-top-throw ACs — though R&D intensity is modest and margins stay thin.
scores.quote: Our dedicated and continuous R&D efforts give us an edge to provide solutions that are first to market

scores.rationale: Serial, escalating M&A (ILJIN/Ever, Ascent, Power-One, Unitronics Israel, Shogini, multiple JVs) did lift electronics EBITDA from ~3% in 2018 to 8.8% in FY26, but these are neither small nor simple, and the Shivalik JV was written off for INR112cr.
scores.quote: exceptional one-off impairment of investment in Shivalik and share of loss of Shivalik JV amounting to INR112 crores

scores.rationale: No buyback, dividend or distribution policy discussed across the excerpts; all capital is redeployed into capex, stake increases and acquisitions.

Working capital is tightly run (9-29 days) but the business is capital-hungry — greenfields, PCB fabs, net debt — and the ~8% EBITDA contract-manufacturing model lacks a protecting moat, with ROCE only reaching the mid-teens after years of promises.
scores.quote: we expect a jump of around 300 basis points in our ROCE level, taking it to above 15% financial year '25

scores.rationale: Documented, continuing share capture — OEM value share rose from 21.2% in FY18 to 26.6% in FY22, and the CD division grew 14% in FY26 against a flat RAC industry.
scores.quote: Our market share in value terms at OEM manufacturing level has increased from 21.2% in FY18... to 26.6% in FY22

scores.rationale: Geographic expansion is mostly domestic multi-plant footprint; exports remain aspirational — the US/European rolling-stock order took four years to reach development stage and needs 2.5 more years.
scores.quote: we have reached to the final stage of receiving our developmental order of air conditioner for trains from the US markets

scores.rationale: Growth is volume- and pass-through-led, not pricing/mix-led, and mix is actively moving down-market with the Oppo assembly entry at 1.5-2% EBITDA.
scores.quote: normally, the industry is operating at 1.5% to 2% of EBITDA levels

scores.rationale: RAC is emerging from a weather-hit trough (Q1/Q2 FY26 down ~30%, full year flat) with a visible upturn — Q1 FY27 industry expected +20% and full year +12-13%.
scores.quote: quarter 1 and quarter 2 were very, very flattish or they were like down by 30%. But quarter 3 and quarter 4 saw the recovery

scores.rationale: End markets are in secular expansion — AC penetration spreading to Tier 3/4 and rural India, and the bare PCB market moving from INR37,000cr to INR80,000cr by 2030 with 85% still imported.
scores.quote: The bare board PCB market in India stands today at INR37,000 crores and is expected to reach INR80,000 crores by 2030

scores.rationale: Strategy is acquisition-led rather than organic — a near-continuous stream of deals and JVs funded with debt (net debt INR965cr in FY25) — though deleveraging to INR511cr and low working capital show some prudence.
scores.quote: we acquired Power-One Microsystems in August, Unitronics in October and Shogini in December

scores.rationale: A consistent 25-year backward-integration vision executed patiently (sheet metal to 70% of BOM) plus four years of persistence on export homologation evidences long-term tenacity.
scores.quote: Every 3 years, we used to add one component as a backward integration... we touched about 70% of bill of material

scores.rationale: Communication is operationally detailed and promoter-led rather than celebrity-driven, but management is highly visible to the street and convened a special call at short notice to publicise the Oppo tie-up.
scores.quote: Business Update Call held at a shorter notice

scores.rationale: Leadership is bought in rather than grown — the PCB division is headed by a hire from AT&S and Ascent's founder-MD exited — with no evidence of a systematic internal pipeline, though bandwidth for new divisions is being planned.
scores.quote: it will be headed the whole division, PCB division will be headed by Mr. Santosh. He has 25 years experience

scores.rationale: Management pre-announces bad news with specifics and owns operating mistakes — flagging 50-100bps margin pressure, explaining railway project delays, and admitting the Tier-2 PCB pass-through lag was a learning.
scores.quote: the lag in the PCB business to increase the cost is about 2 quarters. So this has been our learning in last 1 year

scores.rationale: Headline growth owes much to industry tailwinds, PLI/anti-dumping policy and acquisitions rather than pure skill — PAT of INR338cr on INR12,186cr revenue (~2.8%) and repeatedly deferred ROCE targets separate results from returns.
scores.quote: The recent announcement of government imposing antidumping duty on PCBs up to 6 layers has given the much needed boost

scores.rationale: Claims of being India's only integrated one-stop B2B provider and now the largest PCB manufacturer, plus a small captive AMC/refurb stream at Sidwal, fall short of a monopoly-like hold on the customer's mind.
scores.quote: nobody has the solutions like we have

scores.rationale: Some stickiness from integrated multi-location supply and backward integration, but switching costs are visibly weak — customers benchmark and negotiate, and brands are setting up their own ODM capability.
scores.quote: few of our customers taking that data and they attempted a negotiation bid

scores.rationale: Customers are large, powerful OEM brands who negotiate hard and can in-source; pricing is a quarterly cost pass-through rather than a negotiated-power position.
scores.quote: This will get adjusted in the future quarter in the form of a price increase which will take on the quarterly lag basis

scores.rationale: Management itself concedes room for new entrants, peers are converting to ODM, and Chinese price-cutting forced a strategy change in PCBA — barriers are low and pricing not always rational.
scores.quote: There is certainly room for one or two more new players

scores.rationale: Imports are the donator — 85% of India's PCB demand is imported and anti-dumping duty immediately converted into four new customers, plus in-house OEM capacity being displaced by ODM outsourcing.
scores.quote: 85% of its total demand today is still bring that through the imports

scores.rationale: The opposite of under-the-radar — heavily covered by CLSA, Macquarie, Ambit and others, and operating in the most capital-attracting EMS/PLI theme in India.
scores.quote: Your next question comes from the line of Indrajit A. with CLSA

scores.rationale: No image- or taste-driven pricing power; gross and EBITDA margins are thin (consol ~8%), costs are passed through with a lag, and the newest business runs at 1.5-2% EBITDA.
scores.quote: we expect a margin pressure of 50 to 100 bps at consolidated level

scores.rationale: Customers buy reliability and scale certainty — Oppo's choice was framed explicitly on quality, scale and operational consistency rather than price.
scores.quote: confidence that a global brand of significant standing has placed in our manufacturing capabilities, quality infrastructure, ability to deliver at scale and operational consistency

scores.rationale: Amber's differentiator is accessibility — an integrated one-stop solution delivered across 23 geographies with plants located near customers, and proactive inventory buildup to guarantee supply.
scores.quote: Will they be able to offer the solutions in all the 23 geographies like Amber does

scores.rationale: Entirely corporate customers served with the right levers (TCO, reliability, backward integration), but the lock-in is incomplete since OEMs retain in-house options and negotiate on price.
scores.quote: other players going ahead and they themselves initially consumers of other people

scores.rationale: A genuine multi-product technical layer — first Indian in-house inverter PCB, ODM firsts in tower/cassette ACs, and a move up to HDI PCB and semiconductor substrates — though intensity and pricing capture remain modest.
scores.quote: we became the first company in India to develop our own inverter PCB solutions

scores.rationale: No two-sided network dynamic is present or discussed anywhere in the excerpts.
There is a real manufacturing-footprint reach near customer plants across regions, but no distribution or service network moat in the classic sense for a B2B component supplier.
scores.quote: expanding its manufacturing footprint now in the western region and southern region respectively

scores.rationale: Sustained large growth capex (67.5→109 mt, ~INR7,500 cr in FY26) funded by internal accruals while staying debt-free, but incremental returns are unproven as new/acquired assets run at low utilisation and the 140/155 mt target slipped to FY30.
scores.quote: Capacity growth from the current 89 million tons to 140 million tons will be met through internal accruals and operating cash flows. We will continue to remain debt free

scores.rationale: A&P has been stepped up materially (Adani Cement brand transition, 300 mn reach, CREDAI/BAI platforms, FutureX, 36,000 ACT sites) and coincides with premium cement at 35% of trade sales, though it also visibly inflated Q4 cost per tonne.
scores.quote: the higher branding cost, now that we have focused more on trade sales starting from the Q4

scores.rationale: R&D exists but is early-stage and pilot-scale (Coolbrooks RotoDynamic Heater, Indo-Swedish carbon capture with IIT Bombay, 'R&D-backed customized cements' still promised), with no track record of R&D translating into products or customers.
scores.quote: our R&D -backed customized cement solutions, you will hear it very soon

scores.rationale: M&A has been large and repeated (Sanghi, Penna, Orient, Tuticorin) rather than small bolt-ons, the acquirees were weak assets needing overhaul, and post-deal margins suffered from low utilisation and unplanned maintenance capex.
scores.quote: some of these plants, especially of Penna, needed higher than expected time for maintenance capex and overall upkeep of the assets

scores.rationale: Only a modest dividend (Rs 630 cr outflow in Q1FY25) with no buybacks and no articulated distribution policy — cash is being channelled entirely into capacity and acquisitions.
scores.quote: dividend outflow of Rs. 630 crores and balance towards working capital

scores.rationale: Deeply asset-heavy model with INR6,000–7,500 cr annual capex and acquired capacity running at 46–58% utilisation, so asset turns are structurally low despite the balance-sheet strength.
scores.quote: Sanghi still remains at around, say, at 57% on cement capacity utilization, while Penna is 46%

scores.rationale: Clear runway from a non-dominant base and demonstrated capture — share moved from ~14% to 16.6% with volumes growing at twice the industry rate and a stated 20% target.
scores.quote: growing our volumes at 2x the industry average... the market share improved to 16.6%

scores.rationale: Credible domestic footprint extension into the South (Penna, ACC brands), East and a new Assam limestone block, executed with mixed timing but real capacity on ground; no international expansion.
scores.quote: we have won a limestone block in Assam. Again, that's a completely new territory for us

scores.rationale: Growth is overwhelmingly volume- and acquisition-led with realisations essentially flat (INR254/bag vs INR255 a year earlier), partially offset by genuine mix gains from premium cement at 35–36% of trade sales.
scores.quote: we have sustained the price levels at INR254 a bag... compared to, say, last year, we were at say, INR255

scores.rationale: The company sits mid-cycle rather than near a bottom — FY26 demand grew ~8% but FY27 is guided softer at 5–5.5% with costs at peak and pricing unable to be passed on.
scores.quote: industry is still under the relentless pressure and not able to pass on the price

scores.rationale: End market is in secular expansion, tied to India's ~1.1x GDP cement demand, US$3 trillion infrastructure and housing pipeline, explicitly described by management as structural.
scores.quote: India's long -term infrastructure story remains fundamentally very strong and secular

scores.rationale: Prudent leverage (debt-free, AAA) and a recent pivot to capital discipline are offset by a five-year record of aggressive serial M&A and capacity targets that had to be recalibrated by two years.
scores.quote: the target plans of FY '28, it could move a year or 2, let us say, on a safer side, I would say that FY '30

scores.rationale: A consistent long-term roadmap (capacity, cost per tonne, 1,000 MW green power) has been pursued tenaciously since 2022, but delivery repeatedly lags the stated timelines on both capacity and cost.
scores.quote: I have mentioned earlier about our journey to achieve cost of almost INR4,000 a tonne by March '26 exit... we have achieved a figure of INR4,400 a tonne

scores.rationale: The business is run under one of India's most high-profile promoter groups with deliberate amplification of the Adani Cement brand and Adani family directors on calls — the opposite of low-profile.
scores.quote: we have introduced and more larger a mplification of Adani Cement brand

scores.rationale: Some talent signals — a unified end-to-end management team across entities, a 'younger, digital-savvy' organisation and the FutureX academia programme — but no evidence of a systematic internal leadership pipeline.
scores.quote: our organization is becoming younger... We are becoming more digital savvy

scores.rationale: Management openly flags misses and their causes — cost overruns, project delays, weak acquired-asset ramp-up — and provides apple-to-apple reconciliation tables, though disclosure leans heavily on 'normalized' figures.
scores.quote: we have seen a bit of higher cost compared to our own expectations and therefore, some disappointments

scores.rationale: Headline growth is flattered by acquisitions and one-off items (Himachal excise drawback, tax refunds) and by group adjacencies rather than demonstrated per-tonne operating skill, so results should not be read as proof of management quality.
scores.quote: Unlike if you go with the reported numbers, you will find a steep fall, but that is incorrect because there are exceptional items

scores.rationale: Premium SKUs (Ambuja Kawach, ACC Gold) hold some mind-share, but cement remains a substitutable commodity with no monopoly-like position or aftermarket lock-in.
scores.quote: Ambuja Kawach and ACC Gold, they remain our blockbuster premium cement products

scores.rationale: Freight economics create regional strongholds and micro-market management, but there are no switching costs — the company itself concedes its lead distances are worse than peers in several markets.
scores.quote: my lead is relatively higher compared to the -- some of the peers

scores.rationale: The industry is consolidating meaningfully with the top five moving from ~45% (2018) to ~60% of volumes, though pricing behaviour shows customers still hold bargaining power.
scores.quote: The share of top 5 companies has come to 60 % versus some 45 odd percent in 2018

scores.rationale: High capital and limestone-licence barriers exist, but pricing rationality is poor — historically rollback-prone hikes and an inability to pass through a INR400–500/t cost shock in FY26.
scores.quote: these hikes have helped making a departure from the rollback -prone patterns of the previous years

scores.rationale: Weak players are plainly available as share donators — the company has repeatedly bought distressed capacity (Sanghi, Penna, Orient) and grows volumes at double the industry rate.
scores.quote: Successful amalgamation of Sanghi Industries and Penna Cement with Ambuja Cements is now completed

scores.rationale: This is the single most scrutinised consolidation story in Indian cement, backed by abundant capital and heavy analyst/media attention — the antithesis of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: part of the diversified Adani portfolio and the world's ninth largest building material solutions company

scores.rationale: Brand-led premiumisation is real (35% of trade sales, super-premium SKUs) but has not converted into pricing power, with realisations flat year-on-year and commodity-level margins.
scores.quote: realization has hardly moved Q -o-Q versus for peers, it is up somewhere between 1.5% to 2%

scores.rationale: Legacy Ambuja/ACC trust plus a sizeable technical-services organisation and certified-site programme mean customers are buying reliability and quality assurance, not just price.
scores.quote: What we call it as ACT, Adani Certified Technology site... this quarter, we had almost 36,000 ACT sites

scores.rationale: Strong and improving accessibility and customer intimacy — expanded dealer network, direct-to-customer dispatches raised to 55%, 70,000+ contractor/influencer network and micro-market management.
scores.quote: We have a network of 70,000 -plus contractors, influencers

scores.rationale: The mix is correctly matched — roughly 70–75% retail/trade demand served with brand and premium products, while the shrinking non-trade institutional share is the price-sensitive segment.
scores.quote: my share of trade and non -trade is almost, 65% is trade and non -trade is 35%... Down the line, it will be moving towards 70% -30%

scores.rationale: There are genuine first-mover technology initiatives (Coolbrooks kiln electrification, CiNOC AI operations centre) but they are pilots or efficiency tools, not a deep multi-product edge delivering superior customer benefit.
scores.quote: we have been the first in the universe in terms of the commercial scale installation of Coolbrooks RDH

scores.rationale: No evidence of any self-reinforcing two-sided network in the disclosures.

A deliberately built logistics and service reach — hub-and-spoke grinding units, owned GPWIS/BCFC rakes, vessels, sea route and group adjacencies — though lead distances still trail peers, so the advantage is under construction rather than unmatched.
scores.quote: we have also ordered 26 BCFC rakes... we have already ordered the vessels, almost 7 of them

scores.rationale: Across all 17 excerpts there is no discussion of physical or growth capex — the business is asset-light distribution and investment is in people, not assets.

A&P is essentially absent as a lever; brand equity is described as arising from listing status and client word-of-mouth rather than promotional spend, with business promotion mentioned only as a normalising post-COVID cost.
scores.quote: the brand building happens because of the listing status and vice versa

scores.rationale: A dedicated Product & Research function and simulation-based structured product design (pre-decided designs for different rate/vol regimes) support the offering, but management explicitly avoids frequent product innovation and R&D is not a quantified spend.
scores.quote: we don't innovate every quarter... What will be the product I will launch is already pre-decided

scores.rationale: No acquisitions in five years — growth is entirely organic; the only capital deployment outside the business is a ₹40 crore rights subscription to maintain an 8% stake in group NBFC ARGFL, a related-party top-up rather than a bolt-on.
scores.quote: it has only subscribed to its entitlement... about 8% of that, that was about INR 40 crores

scores.rationale: A coherent, repeated distribution policy — ₹164.65 crore buyback completed FY25, plus 1:1 bonus and ₹7 final dividend in FY26 — though nothing indicates the buyback was timed to a low valuation.
scores.quote: we successfully concluded the buyback program of Rs 164.65 crores

scores.rationale: Extremely asset-light distribution model producing best-in-industry returns (ROE 42.3% in FY23 rising to 46.74% in FY26) with the moat coming from near-zero client attrition.
scores.quote: Return on equity on an annualized basis stood at best in industry at 46.74% for FY '26

scores.rationale: Long runway with demonstrated capture — AUM grew from ₹32,142 crore (Jun-22) to ₹1,06,300 crore (Jun-26) and client families from 7,400 to 13,941, against a stated aspiration of only 3-4% equity MF share.
scores.quote: I will get to 3% - 4% of equity mutual fund market share in India

scores.rationale: Geographic expansion is only just beginning — UK operations were announced in Jul-2026 with no revenue or execution record yet, and no prior international footprint across the earlier calls.
scores.quote: We have also started operations in UK and very soon you all will see this business flowing from there

scores.rationale: Growth is volume/AUM-led rather than price-led: yields are explicitly flat and mildly under pressure from the new SEBI TER structure, with management saying the squeeze has already happened.
scores.quote: Do I see any material change in 1.09, not significant... the squeeze, which was supposed to happen, has happened

scores.rationale: The business is levered to equity markets (AUM mix shifts driven by mark-to-market) but management targets market-agnostic delivery and has grown through both all-time-high and volatile quarters — it is not positioned at a cycle bottom.
scores.quote: we will try and deliver market-agnostic performance

scores.rationale: End market is in secular expansion — rising HNI count in a fast-growing economy, with equity mutual funds at only ~1.8% of Indian household savings versus 28% in gold, implying a long financialisation runway.
scores.quote: gold already is 28% of India's household savings... an equity mutual funds is 1.8%

scores.rationale: Consistently organic, no leverage or big M&A, guidance framed as under-commit/over-deliver; the offset is meaningful related-party concentration in group NBFC ARGFL for structured products plus revaluation gains routed through P&L.
scores.quote: under commit, over deliver... The proportion of Anand Rathi is greater and third party is lower

scores.rationale: Repeated evidence of independent, contrarian long-termism — moving to all-trail voluntarily two years before SEBI mandated it, refusing gold and direct plans, and explicitly rejecting popular industry practices.
scores.quote: we went all trail before SEBI made it mandatory in 2018... we don't do anything because it is popular to do

scores.rationale: Management is notably promotional on calls — self-referential statistics, publishing a 'credibility marathon' slide instructing other industry CEOs, and repeated claims of rarity within the Nifty 500.
scores.quote: We might be one of the few companies in the world who measure the standard deviation of their PAT growth declared

scores.rationale: Systematic internal talent build — 78% of new RMs trained from colleges, sustained zero regret RM attrition across many quarters, and an all-RM leadership structure of 86 team leaders and 19 unit heads.
scores.quote: 78% are people whom we trained from colleges and made them RMs... lateral hires cannot be a substantive portion of your strategy

scores.rationale: Explicit, checkable guidance with owned misses (admitting the ₹1 lakh crore AUM target was not met by 30 March), disclosed RM defections with precise retained-asset numbers, and both reported and adjusted P&L given.
scores.quote: Unfortunately, we didn't meet it on the 30th March number

scores.rationale: Results are genuinely consistent but flattered by a multi-year equity bull market (AUM mix changes attributed to mark-to-market) and by ₹54.6cr/₹96cr non-operating revaluation gains on the related-party NBFC stake, so skill is not cleanly separable from tailwinds.
scores.quote: INR96 crores that is mark-to-market gain in the holding of Anand Rathi Global Finance Limited

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like position — the firm holds only a low-single-digit target share in a crowded field, though it owns strong mindshare within its own client base.
scores.quote: I will get to 3% - 4% of equity mutual fund market share in India

scores.rationale: Real switching costs are evidenced by 0.09-0.54% annual client AUM attrition and 80-90% asset retention even when relationship managers defect to competitors.
scores.quote: 90% of it is retained approximately without the market movement

scores.rationale: The industry is fragmented and contested, with numerous MLD/structured-product issuers and freshly capitalised entrants bidding aggressively for the firm's RMs.
scores.quote: This specific company was wanting to hire people at very obscene salaries because they'd raised some capital

scores.rationale: Low structural barriers — new wealth outfits are launched every couple of years, capital-backed rivals poach talent on price, and regulatory TER changes plus direct plans keep compressing economics.
scores.quote: there's somebody who's wanting to build a wealth management business very quickly

scores.rationale: Abundant weak competitors to take share from — portfolios elsewhere delivering sub-11% IRRs on complex products, rivals with 4-10% client attrition, and two structured product issuers that went belly up.
scores.quote: we have already seen 2 structured product popular issuers in India almost went belly up

scores.rationale: The opposite of under-the-radar — listed since 2021, heavily covered by institutional analysts, actively publicising its playbook to would-be competitors, in a niche capital is chasing.
scores.quote: why don't we make that public information of what has been our learning so far

scores.rationale: Clients pay a full ~1.09% regular-plan commission when free direct plans exist, supporting a 32% PAT margin — pricing power rooted in trust and 'uncomplicated' positioning rather than image or taste.
scores.quote: I don't give direct as an option to even one client if he offers us Rs 2,000 crores... I will not sell myself cheap

scores.rationale: The proposition is explicitly certainty over performance chasing — low-beta (0.6-0.65) portfolios, gatekeeping of intergenerational money, and near-nil client attrition show price is secondary to trust.
scores.quote: We operate highest beta portfolio is 0.6-0.65... you're taking lower risk than Nifty

scores.rationale: Direct client intimacy via a 360+ RM force in which every leader including the Joint CEO personally manages clients, giving unusually deep relationship coverage.
scores.quote: CEO is an RM, joint CEO is RM, unit head is RM, team leader is an RM

scores.rationale: Benefit type is well matched to the customer — HNI retail families are sold assurance and simplicity with intergenerational lock-in, and short-term or non-fitting money is deliberately refused.
scores.quote: We do a very strong gatekeeping in terms of what assets we onboard to manage

scores.rationale: Technology exists (OFA SaaS, Digital Wealth, mathematics-led advice) but is financially immaterial — OFA revenue was ₹1.84 crore in a quarter against total revenue of ₹245 crore.
scores.quote: OFA business reported revenue of Rs 1.84 crores, which is a growth of 18% year-on-year

scores.rationale: The OFA platform is the only two-sided asset and it has plateaued — 6,064 MFD subscribers in Q1FY25, 6,906 in FY26 and 6,890 by Q1FY27 — so no self-reinforcing network is compounding.
scores.quote: OFA business, which is a SaaS platform, has 6,890 subscribers

scores.rationale: Distribution is the core asset — an internally grown RM force (271 in 2022 to 360+ by 2024) with sustained zero regret attrition that rivals cannot buy, though reach is still small in absolute national terms.
scores.quote: My competitors who bid for my RMs, would want to give them twice the salary, but they won't leave

scores.rationale: Almost all capex is growth capex — data centre IT load scaled 3MW→6MW→28MW with 63MW guided by Dec'26 and 117MW by FY28, at ~INR26cr/MW incremental cost against ~INR75 lakh/MW/month EBITDA (≈3-year payback) because land and buildings were already owned, and each milestone (3MW, 6MW, 28MW) was actually delivered on the promised date.
scores.quote: we are incurring an additional expense of INR26 crores which we recover in three years

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in any of the five calls; the only marketing-adjacent event is an investor showcase, not brand-building A&P.
No R&D spend, programme or output is mentioned anywhere across the five calls.

Acquisitions are land parcels rather than operating businesses — 20 acres in Gurgaon at ~INR20cr/acre including a partial buyout of CTG Properties with an external partner retained — bolt-on and complementary to the existing township, but with no acquired earnings stream or post-deal margin evidence to judge.
scores.quote: We spend about INR 20 crores an acre if we translate it in the money terms, average for this.

scores.rationale: The trajectory is repeated issuance, not distribution — INR500cr QIP in Jan'24, a INR2,100cr fundraise plan announced Nov'24 and a INR1,100cr QIP completed in FY26 — with no buyback or dividend policy articulated in any call; the one shareholder-alignment positive is promoters converting INR100cr of warrants at INR730 early.
scores.quote: the company also successfully completed its QIP of INR 1,100 crores which is done

scores.rationale: Structurally asset-heavy on both legs — a ~200-acre Gurgaon land bank plus land and buildings valued near INR3,000cr and ~INR700cr already sunk into data centres — so revenue of ~INR2,100cr sits on a very large asset base, though the pre-owned, unencumbered land is a genuine cost and timeline moat.
scores.quote: the land and the existing buildings which we are sitting on today are at a valuation of close to INR3,000 crores

scores.rationale: Clear runway and demonstrated capture rather than incumbency — revenue went from ~INR200cr about 4.5 years ago to INR2,100cr in FY25, and 28MW of live IT load is a small share of India's data-centre market with 300MW of permitted capacity still to build, but no explicit market-share data is given.
scores.quote: the complete turnover of Anant Raj was 200 crores. And from there, you have seen up to Q2, we have already done 1200 crores

scores.rationale: Expansion is real but domestic and adjacent — Manesar, then Panchkula (7MW), then Rai/Sonipat (20MW of a planned 200MW), affordable housing at Tirupati, and a first Delhi development at Mehrauli after decades confined to Haryana; each step was announced and then executed on schedule.
scores.quote: now in Delhi, we have already started with our first development which is 7 lakh square feet

scores.rationale: Mix and price both contribute — Gurgaon prices rose ~60% and 20% post-launch, the shift into cloud multiplies revenue per MW 4-5x versus colocation, and EBITDA margin improved from 23.5% to 27.2% — but the bulk of the growth still comes from adding acres and megawatts, i.e. volume.
scores.quote: the revenue projections which we have seen on paper is almost four to five times higher than what we are presently getting

scores.rationale: The company was well positioned at the bottom of Gurgaon's 7-9 year downturn that turned in 2021, but by FY26 the NCR cycle is several years into an upturn with prices already up ~60%, so the cyclical entry point is behind rather than ahead.
scores.quote: Gurgaon had gone through a big recession for almost seven to nine years, and this only started changing in 2021

scores.rationale: The data-centre and sovereign-cloud end market is in permanent secular expansion, driven by data-localisation rules and the pending Data Protection Act, a policy tailwind management has cited consistently since the first call in 2023.
scores.quote: this law is here to stay, sir. So, demand here is only going to go up.

scores.rationale: Delivery against a stated deleveraging promise across all five calls — net debt INR988cr (FY23) → INR290cr (FY24) → INR95cr (Sep'24) → net cash, cost of debt from ~20% to below 10%, the first 28MW funded from internal accruals with an explicit refusal to lever up, and no large M&A.
scores.quote: the whole idea is to do this without taking on debt, we are very clear that we do not want to do this by taking debt

scores.rationale: Fourth-generation owner-operators who accumulated land for decades, held it through a nine-year Gurgaon recession, spent four years building the data-centre business before it produced revenue, and self-funded the first cloud pilot from internal sources.
scores.quote: like four years back, we started this data centre thing and now today it is practically happening on ground

scores.rationale: Genuinely low-profile historically — the first-ever earnings call was only held in April 2023 — but the recent posture is more promotional, with the cloud branded 'Ashok Cloud' after the founder chairman, a two-day 'Bharat Built from soil to server' investor showcase, and talk of competing with global hyperscalers.
scores.quote: you are going to be then competing with all the hyperscalers and the largest ones in the world

scores.rationale: The bench visibly widened across the calls — from MD plus CFO in 2023 to a CBO and a next-generation family member, Ashim Sarin, running the data-centre division and later serving as Whole-Time Director and COO — but succession is family-based and no systematic talent programme is described.
scores.quote: Mr. Ashim Sarin, who is also the CEO and the Director of the company and he heads the data center division

scores.rationale: Guidance has generally been met or beaten and stated frankly — FY25 topline guided at INR1,800-1,900cr delivered at INR2,100cr, net-debt-free by Dec'24 achieved — and management admits gaps in its own competence on cloud, though the 2024 promise of 300MW within four years is quietly inconsistent with the current 117MW-by-FY28 plan and is never reconciled.
scores.quote: they will give us all the details because we do not have a lot of expertise in this segment

scores.rationale: Results are hard to separate from tailwinds: a ~60% NCR price surge, land and buildings bought decades ago at legacy cost, and a government data-localisation mandate — management itself attributes the outcome to sector tailwinds and pre-owned assets rather than distinctive operating skill.
scores.quote: This is thanks to the tailwinds in our sector and thanks to RERA and other regulations

scores.rationale: No monopoly in the customer's mind — competition is expected and acknowledged, and the pitch is cost rather than indispensability — though the sovereign-cloud positioning is a genuinely narrow niche with limited qualified suppliers.
scores.quote: of course, when the competition starts kicking in, then things will change

scores.rationale: Colocation creates real switching costs once racks, servers and government workloads are installed — 75% of colocation load is government and capacity is fully pre-tied-up — and the 200-acre contiguous Sector 63A township is effectively a local monopoly position.
scores.quote: Completely tied up, sir, fully tied up, sir.

scores.rationale: Neither end market is a stable oligopoly — NCR residential is fragmented and Indian data centres are attracting well-capitalised entrants including hyperscalers, with management itself conceding future supply and price change.
scores.quote: Of course, supply will be there, but the demand is phenomenally going to increase

scores.rationale: Real entry barriers exist in permissions, power and time — management claims a 3-4 year head start rivals cannot close — but pricing discipline is questionable given the company operates at roughly half of market pricing and expects rentals to reset as competition arrives.
scores.quote: Anybody to be on the stage where we are would take at least three to four years

scores.rationale: Cost-disadvantaged incumbents spending roughly double per megawatt are implicitly the share donators, but no weak competitor is named or quantified anywhere in the calls.
scores.quote: we are able to do this in INR26 crores, sir, whereas there are people who are spending almost double this amount

scores.rationale: The opposite of ignored — Indian data centres are among the most capital-attractive niches, and the company has moved from its first-ever call in 2023 to a INR2,100cr fundraise plan, a INR1,100cr QIP and a two-day analyst showcase, with coverage from Nomura, Motilal Oswal, Kotak and Emkay.
scores.quote: we invited them for 2 days to come and we showcase this

scores.rationale: Some premium positioning in residential (luxury high-rise, Birla Estates JV, 70% end-user demand) but no image-driven pricing power in data centres, where the company explicitly sells at roughly half market price and margins come from low cost rather than brand.
scores.quote: Today, compared to the market, we are almost at 50% cost and even then our margins are pretty good

scores.rationale: Data-centre and sovereign-cloud customers — 75% government in colocation, anchored by RailTel and TCIL — are buying uptime, compliance and data sovereignty rather than price, though the company still leads its pitch with cost.
scores.quote: we are a sovereign Cloud of the country and today's sovereign Cloud has a very niche demand for itself

scores.rationale: Deliberate move up the stack from colocation to servers to Ashok Cloud gives one-stop accessibility for the customer, and the cloud entry itself was pulled in by an existing colocation client — evidence of direct customer intimacy.
scores.quote: today we are a single stop solution for everything

scores.rationale: The benefit type is reasonably matched to each customer — corporate and government buyers get TCO advantage, sovereignty compliance and infrastructure lock-in; retail homebuyers, 70% of whom are end users, get a township and branded JV product.
scores.quote: almost 70% of our sales has been done to end users

scores.rationale: The technology is sourced, not owned — the cloud stack rests on a technical tie-up with Orange, management concedes it lacks segment expertise and relies on a client for handholding, and there is no R&D intensity behind any of it.
scores.quote: the technical tie-up for the product which we have launched so far... is with Orange, the French company

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing dynamic exists — growth comes from adding megawatts and acres, and each incremental customer requires proportional new capital rather than making the platform more valuable to the next one.
scores.quote: one megawatt has an additional investment of close to INR 100 crores

scores.rationale: Channel tie-ups with RailTel and TCIL, both Government of India undertakings, give privileged access to the government workload pool that now makes up 75% of colocation demand — a reach private rivals cannot easily replicate — but it is a partner-dependent rather than owned distribution network.
scores.quote: one with RailTel and one with TCIS, both are Government of India undertaking to help us get clients

scores.rationale: Capex is genuinely growth-oriented but asset-light (tech assets, data centre/DR, cloud) with most incremental capital going into working capital and the client funding book at high returns (ROE ~43%), plus fresh ₹1.5bn infusions each into wealth and NBFC.
scores.quote: Depreciation and amortization costs increased by 27%... on account of augmentation of technology assets at a data center and disaster recovery site

scores.rationale: Large, sustained A&P (5-year IPL associate sponsorship, ~₹1.2bn a season) has built visibility in tier-2/3 India, but management itself was challenged on weak correlation between heavy marketing and growth, so brand-equity payback is unproven.
scores.quote: we have spent heavily on marketing and we correlate that to the growth in the numbers... I am not seeing a growth which is as high as I would have hoped correlating into the marketing

scores.rationale: Continuous in-house product/tech development has repeatedly shipped new revenue lines — Super App, mutual funds/SIP, credit, Ask Angel AI — with 50%+ of engineering AI-augmented, though returns show up as volume rather than pricing power.
scores.quote: more than 50% of development is augmented by AI... A testament of this is the transformation of Ask Angel itself

scores.rationale: No acquisitions are discussed across the period; every new business (AMC, Ionic Wealth, NBFC/credit) was built organically with hired teams, so there is no M&A track record to judge.

Distribution policy is coherent but subordinated to growth — an initial 35% payout, then dividends deferred in FY24 to fund working capital, resumed at ₹1/share in FY27, with no buybacks at any valuation.
scores.quote: the Board has decided to defer the dividend payout for the next few quarters to conserve resources, optimize our balance sheet and support our growth trajectory

scores.rationale: Genuinely asset-light platform economics sustain ~43-44% ROE, but the balance sheet is becoming heavier as the client funding book (₹71.5bn period-end) and borrowings scale, and the protecting moat is only moderate.
scores.quote: our FY '24 return on average equity remains healthy at 43.3%

scores.rationale: Demat market share rose from 10.8% (Jun 2022) to 16.7% (Mar 2026) with retail equity turnover share sustained above 20% and cash share improving to 17.4%, with participation still low nationally — clear share capture with runway.
scores.quote: further strengthened our demat market share to 16.7%, higher by 54 bps year-over-year

scores.rationale: Expansion is domestic-deepening into tier-2/3 India rather than cross-border, executed well (95% of acquisitions from tier-2/3, AMC folios across 17,575 PIN codes, 45% of Ionic clients non-metro), so no evidence of a brand that travels internationally.
scores.quote: 95% of these clients came from Tier-2, Tier-3 cities

scores.rationale: Growth is overwhelmingly volume- and client-acquisition-led on a flat-fee (discount) price plan with falling revenue per client; the only favourable element is mix diversification toward interest and distribution income.
scores.quote: The average revenue per customer for the quarter was Rs. 453. This was primarily due to a higher share of new-to-market clients

scores.rationale: The business is clearly cyclical and the F&O regulatory tightening plus weak markets created a trough in FY25-26, from which orders have recovered (5mn/day Feb'25 to 7.4mn/day Mar'26) — positioned after the bottom with an identifiable upturn.
scores.quote: Average daily orders scaled from 5 million in February '25 to 7.4 million in March '26... marking a six-quarter high

scores.rationale: The end market — financialization of Indian household savings with very low equity participation among a young, digitally-connected population — is in genuine multi-decade secular expansion, a theme management has articulated consistently since 2022.
scores.quote: equity participation and ownership remains low, leaving a long runway for growth

scores.rationale: Strictly organic build-out with no acquisitions, calibrated scaling of credit, and continued investment through the FY25-26 downturn, though leverage/working capital and a ₹15bn QIP show growth funding needs and dividend deferral.
scores.quote: We are not pursuing growth at the expense of returns, while investment is evaluated through the lens of scalability, profitability and long-term shareholder value creation

scores.rationale: Promoter Dinesh Thakkar has driven a consistent multi-year thesis — flat-fee migration, Super App, then a multi-product AI-led platform — and stuck with it through regulatory and market shocks over the 22 calls.
scores.quote: That is why we remain in a continuous build mode because great fintech business are built by compounding intelligence over time

scores.rationale: Management is deliberately high-profile — five-year IPL associate sponsorship, mass media advertising and grandiose self-description on calls — the opposite of substance-over-celebrity low-profile stewardship.
scores.quote: In the financial technology industry where innovation is the currency of progress, Angel One has stood as a beacon of excellence for three decades

scores.rationale: Leadership is built by lateral hiring rather than an internal pipeline, and the five-year record shows heavy churn — CEO, multiple MDs, wealth and AMC heads exiting, with AMC on an interim CEO by Jul 2026.
scores.quote: if I compare the top management and particularly AMC, we've seen a massive churn in your top management

scores.rationale: Disclosure is clear on costs and normalized versus reported margins including one-offs, but the company repeatedly declines granular disclosure analysts ask for quarter after quarter (client acquisition cost, wealth segment revenue/cost) and avoids owning misses.
scores.quote: Any color on -- again, and I ask this every quarter, but not getting these numbers

scores.rationale: Much of the FY23-24 record reflects an industry-wide F&O boom rather than distinctive skill — profits and margins compressed sharply once F&O regulation landed, and management framing attributes cyclical outcomes to strategy.
scores.quote: This strong recovery reflects resilience of our business amidst a softer macro backdrop due to geopolitical events like global trade tariffs, ongoing wars, full implementation of F&O regulations

scores.rationale: Discount broking is a crowded, comparison-shopped category where Angel is one of several large players with no monopoly-like hold on the customer's mind; its own share of retail turnover is only ~20%.
scores.quote: We sustained a 20.4% share of overall retail equity turnover

scores.rationale: Switching costs in broking are low (accounts are portable and clients hold multiple), and the multi-product cross-sell lock-in management describes is still aspirational rather than demonstrated captivity.
scores.quote: A user may begin their relationship with us through trading and investing, later adopt mutual funds, seek credit as their financial needs grow

scores.rationale: The industry has consolidated toward a handful of large digital brokers, but the end customer retains full negotiating power through free/near-free pricing alternatives, so it is a concentrated but not customer-captive structure.
scores.quote: The net broking revenue under the flat fee plan continued to witness very strong momentum, thereby contributing to a significant 85% of our overall net broking revenue

scores.rationale: Entry barriers are low-to-moderate and pricing is structurally discounted (flat-fee migration, mass acquisition spend), with regulators repeatedly resetting the economics — not a rational, stable-ownership industry.
scores.quote: For 39 months in a row since migrating to a flat pricing structure, we have experienced growth in our average daily orders

scores.rationale: Angel's steady demat and turnover share gains come at the expense of weaker legacy full-service and sub-scale brokers, evidenced by incremental demat share far above its stock share.
scores.quote: On an incremental Demat account basis, our market share expanded to 17.5%

scores.rationale: This is the opposite of an ignored niche — a listed, heavily analyst-covered fintech in India's most capital- and competition-attracting sector, buying IPL sponsorship for maximum visibility.
scores.quote: We have secured the associate partner sponsorship for the coveted India Premier League (IPL) for five years starting in 2024

scores.rationale: There is no image- or taste-driven pricing power: the model is explicitly flat-fee/low-price with declining revenue per client, and demand proved sensitive to regulation and market conditions.
scores.quote: Share of the total net income from our flat fee clients to the consolidated total net income, grew 1.7x to 84%

scores.rationale: Trust, uptime and security are genuinely emphasised and clients were reimbursed for a market-infrastructure disruption, but price and app convenience — not certainty — remain the primary purchase driver in retail broking.
scores.quote: Trust is the currency of all fintech platforms. We continue to operate with a security by design approach

scores.rationale: Convenience is the core proposition and is executed strongly — Super App, KYC 2.0 with faster onboarding, AI assistant, plus an assisted-business channel-partner network reaching non-metro clients directly.
scores.quote: We further optimized client on-boarding journey through a refreshed KYC 2.0... It helps onboard clients faster

scores.rationale: The customer base is almost entirely retail, but the benefit delivered is convenience and low price rather than intangible brand pull, so the benefit-to-customer match is only partial.
scores.quote: Today, with over 38 million registered users, we are already seeing this play out

scores.rationale: A deep, in-house, multi-product tech stack built consistently over five years — broadcast system brought in-house, Super App, platform-level AI with agentic guardrails — though rivals in Indian fintech field comparable capability.
scores.quote: We are moving decisively from isolated AI use cases to platform-level AI integration, rearchitecting both client experiences and internal workflows

scores.rationale: Management claims a data flywheel rather than a genuine two-sided network — more users produce more data, but no user's value rises because another user joined.
scores.quote: Higher engagement leads to richer data, richer data power smarter AI and smarter AI enables more relevant experiences

scores.rationale: Distribution reach is a real strength — 38mn registered users, digital reach into tier-2/3 and 17,575 PIN codes, plus the NXT channel-partner assisted network contributing ~23% of net broking revenue — but it is replicable by well-funded digital rivals.
scores.quote: we are transforming the NXT application, a universal platform for all our channel partners

scores.rationale: Multi-year greenfield Kheda build (Rs115cr Phase 1, then Phase 2a/2) was promised in 2022 and delivered on schedule, lifting group capacity from ~Rs400cr to Rs1,200cr of revenue at a maintained ROCE of ~21%, and management is now explicitly pausing further capacity capex.
scores.quote: we have completed the Phase 2 expansion at Kheda... capacity to generate about INR450 crores revenue per year... We do not foresee any major capex soon for our organic growth

scores.rationale: Promotion is limited to B2B credential-building — trade exhibitions, customer plant visits and a Dubai sales head — with no brand-equity spend of the kind judged like capex.
scores.quote: we intend to do it in certain forums including global multinational exhibitions as well as one on one meetings with the customers

scores.rationale: New product capability comes from in-licensed technology (Graham, Lummus, Brembana & Rolle) on which it pays ~1.3% royalty rather than proprietary R&D, though the tie-ups have yielded real new products and orders.
scores.quote: royalty of about 1.3% as we had many licensed proprietary equipment... mainly helical heat exchangers for Lummus Heat Transfer and EMBaffle heat exchangers for Brembana & Rolle

scores.rationale: Mabel Engineers is exactly the right shape — small, complementary bolt-on — but it materially underdelivered the promise of doubling to Rs100cr in FY26, ending at Rs43cr.
scores.quote: For 26, as I said, we maintain, Mabel will double the turnover to Rs. 100 crores in FY26

scores.rationale: No discussion of dividends, buybacks or any distribution policy across the excerpts.
This is a capital- and working-capital-heavy fabricator: working capital turns fell to 2.2–2.3x against a 3x target, with debtors ballooning and cash turning negative, the opposite of asset-light.
scores.quote: The average working capital was at 2.3 turns. Of course, this could have been better. We would like to maintain it about 3 turns

scores.rationale: Anup is one of only four credible Indian players in a large market and has visibly captured share — order sizes crossing Rs100cr and entry into nuclear, thermal power and precision components — leaving plenty of runway without dominance.
scores.quote: we are now amongst the leading 4 competitors in India for this work and we will be encountering more of these large orders

scores.rationale: Exports went from ~10% of the order book in FY23 to 53.4% of revenue by 9M FY26, backed by a Dubai sales head and wins in US, Middle East, Australia and Nigeria — a promise made in 2022 and actually delivered.
scores.quote: Our exports was at INR328 crores, which is 53.4% of our revenue

scores.rationale: Growth has been capacity/volume-led with fixed-price contracts squeezed by raw-material inflation — EBITDA margin fell from 24.5% in FY22 to ~21% in FY26 — so pricing has been a headwind, not the engine, despite a favourable mix shift toward services.
scores.quote: our contracts are all fixed price contracts... the input cost, especially the raw material cost, is at a quite elevated level

scores.rationale: FY26 was a trough year of stalled US projects and weak order booking, with identifiable upturn drivers now visible — the India-US trade deal, 14GW of revived thermal power and a record Rs1,200cr enquiry bank.
scores.quote: Thermal power projects, which were written off are back strongly with over 14 gigawatts in India

scores.rationale: End markets straddle cyclical oil & gas (still 39%) and genuinely secular ones — hydrogen, nuclear/SMRs, energy storage, fertilizer and energy-security-driven capex — giving partial rather than pure structural expansion.
scores.quote: accelerated push to nonconventional energy sources, which are cleaner, namely nuclear, renewables, green hydrogen

scores.rationale: Growth has been overwhelmingly organic with one tiny bolt-on, modest long-term debt of Rs52cr, and a deliberate choice to forgo order volume to protect margins rather than chase the topline.
scores.quote: we would have reported even better order book numbers as we let go opportunities to protect our financials

scores.rationale: The three-phase Kheda plan laid out in Aug 2022 was executed largely as described over four years and the long-sought nuclear entry finally landed, though senior churn (CEO and CFO exits, multiple chairman changes) tempers the continuity.
scores.quote: we were wanting to get into this for many, many years now... after having put up our facilities and capabilities in place, we thought it is the right time now to move into nuclear

scores.rationale: Calls are run by a single operating MD with sober, detail-heavy commentary and no celebrity framing or promotional flourish, even in the best quarters.
scores.quote: My sincere thanks to all our hard-working committed team members, our partners, our suppliers, and all our shareholders for standing by and trusting in us

scores.rationale: There is evidence of capability-building — ESOPs exercised broadly by staff, a Vadodara design office stabilised into a profit centre, and a dedicated org structure created for the services vertical — but no articulated succession pipeline.
scores.quote: Our design office at Vadodara has stabilized well... It has also started taking small profit center work

scores.rationale: Management repeatedly owns shortfalls unprompted — working capital, Mabel's miss, the Q4 margin dip — walks through cost lines item by item, and withholds FY27 guidance rather than issue a number it cannot stand behind.
scores.quote: On the working capital management, I believe we could have done better

scores.rationale: Strong headline growth is partly the mechanical result of new capacity and an energy capex upcycle, and skill-independent slippage is visible — the Rs1,000cr FY26 target became Rs822cr, Mabel missed, PAT margin fell 2.4pp — so results should not be read as pure managerial skill.
scores.quote: in FY26, when look at FY26, Ahmedabad facility will be at Rs. 600 crores... Kheda... Rs. 300 crores and Mabel will chip in at Rs. 100 crores

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like position exists; the aftermarket/services play (Anup Technical Services) is genuinely promising at ~40% margins but is only ten small orders old and unproven.
scores.quote: We've executed close to about 10 POs now. Of course, not a big amount, close to about INR4.5 crores kind of a value

scores.rationale: Real switching costs exist through customer approvals, stage-wise quality qualification and exclusive licensed designs — the Graham exclusivity gives right of first refusal on their global projects.
scores.quote: we are now the exclusive manufacturers for their global projects. In short, we have the first chance for refusal

scores.rationale: The industry is a narrow field of four Indian players, but the end customers are large refiners and EPCs holding all the negotiating power via fixed-price tenders, and management flags aggressive competition.
scores.quote: we are also seeing some aggressive market competition

scores.rationale: Entry barriers are genuine (approvals, credentials, exotic materials, 200MT single-piece capability), but pricing is not rational — Anup must walk away from work to defend margins and faces global bidders on Indian projects.
scores.quote: there is global competition which is being faced by us here in India for Indian projects

scores.rationale: No weak or retreating competitors are identified anywhere; the commentary describes competitive intensity rising rather than rivals donating share, with wins coming from new segments instead.
scores.quote: we see the competitive intensity kind of increasing in this space

scores.rationale: A modest-sized Ahmedabad fabricator in an unglamorous niche, run without fanfare and rarely the subject of capital-market attention beyond a handful of small-cap funds.
scores.quote: Warm greetings from Team Anup. I sincerely thank you all for your presence on this call

scores.rationale: Gross margins are respectable (~44%) and credentials carry weight, but there is no image- or taste-driven pricing power — fixed-price contracts pass raw-material inflation straight to Anup's P&L.
scores.quote: That would be the material cost of the orders which got impacted worth to the tune of close to 56%, the gross margin at around 44%

scores.rationale: Customers buy certainty in mission-critical equipment — every stage is customer-quality-inspected, credentials accumulate with each dispatch, and nuclear/NPCIL entry required years of proven capability — though price still decides many tenders.
scores.quote: it goes through the customer quality point at every stage

scores.rationale: Customer intimacy is real and improving — free-form accommodation like storing finished goods for customers, a Vadodara design office, a Dubai marketing head and on-site technical services.
scores.quote: customers have requested us to store it for additional 3 months, and we are being paid for those storage char[ges]

scores.rationale: The customer base is entirely corporate/EPC and the benefit stack is correctly matched — reliability, approvals and qualification-based lock-in rather than consumer intangibles — now extended into aftermarket services on the installed base.
scores.quote: health tech assessment of the equipment, providing entity services and repairs of the equipment at site

scores.rationale: Manufacturing capability is genuinely advanced (clean room, exotic materials, 200MT single-piece equipment) but the differentiated process technology is licensed in from Lummus, Graham and Brembana & Rolle, so the edge is executional rather than proprietary.
scores.quote: we are also looking for collaborations and support on the technology and design side with companies and established players in the world

scores.rationale: No two-sided network or self-reinforcing scale dynamic is discussed anywhere in the calls.
This is a shop-fabrication project business with no distribution network; the nascent site-service and Dubai presence is a start but not reach rivals cannot match.
scores.quote: with our presence in Middle East, we have sales and marketing head positioned in Dubai

scores.rationale: Large brownfield growth capex (Rs 250cr FY23 scaling to a Rs 670cr program and Rs 315cr in FY26) was executed and completed with low maintenance needs, but incremental returns lagged badly — revenue fell 34% in Q1FY25 mid-build and FY26 gross block of ~Rs 2,500cr supports only ~Rs 1,676cr standalone revenue (peak Rs 3,500cr), so asset productivity is modest rather than high-ROIC.
scores.quote: we have a gross block of around INR2.5 -- INR2,500 crores... What is the potential peak revenue... we should be looking at about INR3,500 crores

scores.rationale: No mention of advertising or promotional spend in any excerpt — it is a B2B custom-synthesis model.

R&D has consistently converted into commercialised molecules and new revenue streams — team scaled from 85 professionals in FY23 to a pipeline of 65+ molecules, with 12+ commercialised in one year and pharma revenue up 15-fold from Rs 21cr (FY22) to Rs 339cr (FY26).
scores.quote: The Pharma and Polymer pipelines remain strong with 65 plus molecules across R&D and pilot stages

scores.rationale: Tanfac was a genuinely complementary backward-integration bolt-on that delivered, but the cadence has escalated to a US acquisition (Jayhawk, $76mn revenue) and a debt-funded 43-48% stake plus open offer in Bliss GVS — a formulations business running at only 30% utilisation, which is neither small, simple, nor already strong.
scores.quote: this company is today having an operating capacity utilization of only 30%

scores.rationale: No buyback, dividend or distribution policy is discussed in any excerpt; capital allocation is entirely capex, acquisitions and debt.

The business is structurally asset- and working-capital heavy — roughly 1.4x peak asset turn on gross block plus consolidated working capital intensity of ~250 days and Rs 1,500cr gross debt, well short of an asset-light profile.
scores.quote: we are around about working capital intensity for the consolidated would be around about 250-odd days

scores.rationale: Evidence of genuine wallet-share capture from a small base — Japan grew from 1% of revenue in 2018 to 17% by Q3FY26, new MNC customers were added each year, and performance materials grew 245% YoY in 9MFY26.
scores.quote: in 2018, we had just 1% revenue from Japan... as of Q1 FY23, this market contributes 13% to our revenues

scores.rationale: Multi-year, deliberately staffed geographic build-out has been delivered — local BD teams in Japan/Europe/US, Japan now ~17% of revenue, exports 58%, and onshore US manufacturing secured via Jayhawk.
scores.quote: With this acquisition, Anupam will get a direct onshore manufacturing presence in the US

scores.rationale: Contracts are explicitly cost-plus with full pass-through, so there is no pricing power; growth is volume- and mix-driven and mix improvement has not defended margins, which slipped from 28% (Q1FY23) to 22-23% (FY26).
scores.quote: our contract is structured on a cost-plus basis... all costs including raw materials, freight, energy, commodities... are on a passthrough basis

scores.rationale: The agrochem destocking trough of FY25 has clearly passed and the upturn is now visible, with FY26 consolidated revenue up 65% and management describing a healthy revival in offtake.
scores.quote: Agro demand has shown a clear recovery supported by improving channel inventory levels

scores.rationale: A meaningful share of the portfolio now sits in secular end markets — pharma KSM import substitution, semiconductors, EV/LiPF6, electronic materials and defence — though agrochem at 55% of standalone revenue remains the cyclical majority.
scores.quote: presence across agrochemicals, pharma, personal care, performance materials, semiconductors and EV-related applications

scores.rationale: Stewardship has drifted from organic focus to three acquisitions in four years, the latest a Rs 300cr NCD-funded stake in an unrelated formulations company, on top of Rs 1,500cr gross debt and 250-day working capital.
scores.quote: The transaction will be funded through a combination of approximately INR300 crores via non-convertible debentures

scores.rationale: There is real long-horizon tenacity — a decade-long build in Japan, a fluorination platform pursued from identification through backward integration to LiPF6 contracts, and multi-year customer qualification efforts that finally converted.
scores.quote: an effort of over years together to work with a multinational company like that and references that we have created

scores.rationale: The team is technically-oriented and not personality-driven, but commentary leans on promotional framing ('landmark year', 'Make in India', 'Make in America') and heavily marketed headline numbers.
scores.quote: thus contributing to Make in India and Atmanirbhar Bharat campaign

scores.rationale: Consistent senior hiring in R&D and international BD and a stated policy of retaining acquiree management, but no evidence of a systematic internal pipeline — and the FY25 record shows unusual churn across the MD/CEO/CFO roles.
scores.quote: we will continue to work with the same team that is there and support and expand the team as required

scores.rationale: Repeated bullish guidance went undelivered without acknowledgment — FY23 promises of 'strong growth' on Rs 2,620cr of LOIs and $220-260mn of fluorination revenue preceded a 34% revenue collapse blamed wholly on external channel destocking, with no ownership of the misjudgement.
scores.quote: we are very confident of delivering a strong growth in the current financial year on our existing product portfolio

scores.rationale: The FY26 'highest ever revenue' headline is flattered by a depressed base, Tanfac/Jayhawk consolidation and inorganic scale rather than underlying skill — EBITDA margin fell to 23% and PAT margin to 9% versus 28% EBITDA in FY23.
scores.quote: FY '26 has been a landmark year for Anupam Rasayan as we delivered our highest ever revenue

scores.rationale: Multi-step complex chemistry plus long customer qualification cycles create effectively sole-source positions on specific molecules, though not a monopoly in any broad customer mind-space.
scores.quote: high entry barrier chemistry, complex multi-step synthesis, and long-term qualification customer cycles

scores.rationale: Genuine switching costs exist — customers must revalidate molecules over long periods, and Jayhawk was bought explicitly for validations that take years for any competitor to replicate.
scores.quote: they have validation with lot of very high end customers in US, which typically takes a long period for any company to get validated

scores.rationale: This is a fragmented CSM/CDMO market facing Chinese capacity additions, and the end customers are large MNC innovators with clear negotiating power — evidenced by cost-plus contracts and the ability to defer offtake at will.
scores.quote: These degrowth on account of lower volume offtake in Agrochemical segment

scores.rationale: Chemistry complexity and qualification cycles are real barriers, but the FY25 downturn showed exposure to China capacity additions and pricing dominance, and management competes partly on continuous cost-curve reduction rather than pure rationality.
scores.quote: there has been new capacity additions happening in China, which is putting pressure in terms of incremental growth

scores.rationale: Share is available from Chinese and other incumbent suppliers as customers de-risk supply chains and seek import substitution, which management explicitly targets in pharma KSMs and LiPF6.
scores.quote: US players increasingly seeking Indian suppliers for LiPF6 to diversify from SEOC countries

scores.rationale: The chemistries are niche and unglamorous, but the company is a well-covered listed midcap with an EY-run IR programme and analysts from Axis, JM, Investec and Emkay on every call — not ignored by capital.
scores.quote: reach out to E&Y, our investor relation partner

scores.rationale: There is no image- or taste-driven pricing power; contracts are explicit cost-plus pass-throughs and margins compressed from 28% to 22-23% as mix and volumes shifted.
scores.quote: EBITDA, including other income, was at INR141 crores... translating to an EBITDA margin of 22% for this quarter

scores.rationale: Assurance is the core proposition — the company held strategic inventory at customer request through the 2022 supply crisis, backward-integrated into Tanfac for HF/KF security, and wins business on supply-chain credibility rather than price.
